Local LLM Finder

Methodology

How the finder makes its estimates

Last updated 28 September 2026

Memory fit

The finder starts with an illustrative quantized model-weight size, adds estimated runtime and context memory, and leaves a small memory reserve. A result is treated as fitting only when that total stays within the selected planning budget.

Mac and RAM-only estimates

For Mac and “not sure” modes, the tool uses a conservative portion of system memory as the available model-memory budget. This is a planning shortcut rather than a measurement of what macOS or a particular runtime will make available.

Task fit

Task-fit scores are prototype comparison scores, not standard benchmark results. The selected main use receives 65% of the task-fit weighting. Any secondary uses share the remaining 35%, so they can influence the shortlist without overtaking the job the user said matters most. These scores should eventually be replaced or supplemented with sourced evaluation data.

Advanced model filters

Power-user controls can restrict the catalogue to a selected quantization, model family or maximum estimated model-weight file size. These filters do not make a model more compatible; they only narrow the candidates considered. Manual memory override replaces the normal device-derived memory budget and disables device-specific speed estimates.

Speed

When a known graphics card is selected, the tool produces a rough tokens-per-second range using a bandwidth-based proxy and model size. It does not model every factor that affects inference and should not be presented as a measured benchmark.

Model catalogue

The catalogue contains model identities and approximate configurations selected for comparison. Model publishers remain the authoritative source for current model cards, context limits, licences and release information.

What should improve next

The highest-value future data improvement is to replace prototype performance and quality inputs with sourced records that include the measurement hardware, runtime, quantization, context, source date and confidence.
